paragraphs: In a warm city where the streets glowed at sunset, there lived a learned man.
He liked quiet evenings when the air felt soft and still.
One night, he sat on a balcony.
Across the courtyard was a bright house.
And beside him, his shadow stretched long on the ground.
“Look,” the learned man said softly, as if speaking to himself.
Not just the way shadows move.
But as if it were deciding.
It slipped away from the learned man.
And disappeared into the bright house.
But the shadow did not return.
The learned man felt oddly lighter.
As if a quiet companion had gone away.
And one day, a visitor arrived.
“Do you remember me?” the visitor asked.
The learned man felt a chill.
Because the visitor did not feel like a shadow anymore.
He felt like someone in charge.
He knew how to charm a room.
And the learned man—quiet and thoughtful—was ignored.
It will be easier that way.”
Because a shadow is meant to follow.
But the world can be dazzled by confidence.
So the learned man made a choice.
He protected what was true inside him.
And in the quiet of his own room, he remembered something important:
That the brightest voice is not always the wisest.
That the boldest presence is not always the kindest.
And that we must not let anything—
take the place of our true selves.
And he held onto what mattered.
Even when the world was noisy.
